A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same weight-decay and language-model-plasticity study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison across the 28-page v1 and 32-page v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining and fine-tuning experiments, linear probing, attention-rank measurements, and training–validation gap analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds commonsense and safety evaluations, hyperparameter sweeps, stability analyses, and parameter-norm measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions investigate AdamW pretraining weight decay followed by supervised fine-tuning using the same Llama-2 and OLMo-2 architectures. The added experiments do not introduce a new training algorithm, architecture, objective, or adaptation component.

E1.justification: v2 adds fine-tuning on HellaSwag, Winogrande, PiQA, Arc-Easy, and Arc-Challenge, plus safety alignment using Alpaca and safety instructions with evaluation on I-MaliciousInstructions (Appendix C.3–C.4). The original six CoT tasks, pretraining corpora, and SST/AG News probing tasks remain.

E2.justification: v1's Table 3 includes only positive pretraining weight-decay values. v2 adds an explicit no-weight-decay control, λ = 0, for all five model groups and reports its results in appendix comparisons. The existing model families and positive-decay comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces joint pretraining weight-decay/learning-rate sweeps and fine-tuning learning-rate/weight-decay/batch-size sweeps (Appendix E). New protocols include cloze accuracy, harmfulness scoring on 100 prompts with four safety-training sample sizes, and upstream evaluation before and after fine-tuning. The original CoT splits and default fine-tuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests whether the plasticity effect survives changes to other pretraining and fine-tuning hyperparameters, including selection of the best fine-tuning configuration. Appendix D adds stability–plasticity and upstream-performance analyses, while Appendix F.3 adds layer-wise parameter-norm analysis. The original probing, attention-rank, and leave-one-out analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new safety-alignment plots include error bars around mean harmfulness scores (Figures 12–16), but their statistical definition and run/seed counts are unspecified. The existing Pearson leave-one-out analysis is retained as Figure 10, formerly Figure 9.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new tasks, zero-decay controls, hyperparameter sweeps, stability trade-offs, and norm measurements. Existing results also change: the overall Greedy probing/downstream correlation is 0.93 in v1 Figure 15 and 0.87 in v2 Figure 25, alongside an expanded set of model variants. Figure 4(c)'s OLMo probing curves are also revised.

T1.justification: The AdamW equations are rearranged and reindexed but express the same combined update. The attention-rank argument, training–validation gap, and 95%-singular-value pseudo-rank definition are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the three central contributions: stronger pretraining weight decay improves plasticity; minimizing pretraining loss need not optimize downstream performance; and representation, attention-rank, and overfitting effects offer potential mechanisms. The enlarged experiments strengthen support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly distinguishes correlational mechanisms from the experimentally isolated weight-decay effect and discusses sparse model configurations and untested regimes. Appendix D interprets observed stability costs. Its claim that upstream performance is unaffected is overbroad: the listed OLMo-2-1B-140x accuracy falls from 0.61 to 0.56 across decay settings.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-specific Models and Code links, a direct MMLUProCoT source reference, explicit OLMo checkpoint selection for fine-tuning, and detailed sample sizes, safety-training mixtures, and hyperparameter grids. These substantially extend v1's documentation of basic training recipes and hardware. The PDFs establish the presence of access links, not their external availability.

R1.justification: The main related-work section remains largely unchanged. v2 adds references for the new benchmarks and safety setup, vision-pretraining findings, and compositional generalization. Appendix A sharpens the comparison with Kobayashi et al. and expands the connection to the already-cited Lee et al. study.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and portions of the methods and results, particularly Section 4.3, and reorganizes fine-tuning and evaluation material into task-based Appendix C. It adds discussion and analysis sections, while preserving the six-section main narrative and much of the original prose.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to a two-column conference layout. Numerous new experimental figures are added; v1 Figures 10–14 are consolidated into v2 Figure 24. Figure 6 is redesigned to display training loss, validation loss, and their gap, with additional revisions to panels, axes, legends, and captions elsewhere.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence that the plasticity finding extends beyond CoT tasks and is robust to other training choices. Appendix E directly addresses v1's reliance on mostly fixed hyperparameters, while stability analyses, explicit mechanistic limitations, and project access links improve interpretation and reproducibility. Undefined safety error bars and Appendix D's overbroad upstream-performance interpretation are weaknesses, but they do not outweigh these substantial gains.
